subject: Medistruct onboarding: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service-account sequencing
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medistruct.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Medistruct onboarding: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service-account sequencing

Hi Alex / Sally —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our readout, I wanted to lock down the implementation sequence so your infra and security teams have a clean cutover plan. High level we recommend:

1) Sandbox SAML (IdP) test + SCIM provisioning in a dev org
2) Service-account provisioning and least-privilege role map
3) IP allowlist & outbound egress constraints for the prod account
4) Cutover window + rollback steps

A few questions to confirm before Ben and Neha start the config work:
- Which IdP vendor and SAML metadata format will you provide? (raw metadata XML or Okta metadata URL)
- Do you have an IP CIDR range for the allowlist (we can support range + single IPs)?
- Any SCIM custom attribute mappings (e.g., employee_type, cost_center) we should include in the initial sync?

I've attached a short worksheet to capture the answers — please fill the shaded fields and return. Ben will ingest for the service-account mapping and Neha will propose a cutover timeline.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm metadata + allowlist range by EOD Thu
- We: send a 60‑minute technical kickoff invite and share the precheck runbook

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
--
Attachment: medistruct_saml_scim_requirements.xlsx (worksheet, 1 sheet)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medistruct.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@medistruct.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medistruct onboarding: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service-account sequencing

Thanks Grace —

Quick answers inline and attached a filled copy of the worksheet.

- IdP: Okta (we'll share the metadata URL and a signing cert; we use SHA256).
- IP allowlist: Prod egress originates from a fixed NAT pool: 198.51.100.0/27 and two static jump hosts 198.51.200.23, 198.51.200.24
- SCIM: we need employee_type and cost_center mapped; we also send manager_dn for org hierarchy sync.

One more constraint: our security team requires dedicated service accounts per environment (dev/stage/prod) and an audit log of any token creation. Can Redwood generate and rotate service-account keys via our KMS integration?

I've looped Sally (cloud infra lead) onto the thread — she'll join the kickoff call.

Attached: medistruct_saml_scim_requirements.xlsx (filled)

- Alex
Alex Rivera
Platform Engineering Lead, Medistruct
alex.rivera@medistruct.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medistruct.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@medistruct.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medistruct onboarding: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service-account sequencing

All —

Thanks Alex for the details, good to see Okta and the CIDR. A few technical notes from the service side:

- Okta metadata URL works fine; please ensure the HTTPS cert is trusted. We support SHA256 and the usual SAML bindings (HTTP-POST).
- IP allowlist: we will stage the CIDR in a test rule and then push a prod rule during the cutover window. We can accept the two static jump hosts as single-IP allowlist entries.
- SCIM mappings: we can map employee_type and cost_center, and ingest manager_dn into the 'manager' attribute in our user model. If Medistruct plans to use groups-to-roles mapping, note that group sync runs hourly by default (configurable).
- Service accounts: Redwood can create named service accounts per env and rotate keys using customer KMS via an IAM role assumption flow. Neha, we'll need the KMS ARN and a short IAM trust policy snippet from Medistruct to test rotation.

I've attached a first-pass service-account mapping CSV (svcacct-mapping-v1.csv). It lists the minimal permissions we recommend for the provisioning service account and the SSO connector account. Please review and comment.

Recommended cutover cadence (draft):
- Day -7: SCIM dry-run in dev, validate attribute mapping, group/role sanity checks
- Day -3: SAML test in staging with Okta test app (no provisioning)
- Day 0: IP allowlist change + production SAML switch (30m maintenance window)
- Day +1: Audit sweep and token rotation check

Grace — are you able to run the kickoff at 10:00 AM PT Thu (28 Apr) or would Fri work better?

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
--
Attachment: svcacct-mapping-v1.csv (CSV, sample role-to-account map)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Medistruct onboarding: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service-account sequencing

Hi all —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Confirming the kickoff: Thu 29 Apr 10:00 AM PT (note: Alex's team is on PDT — confirmed). Agenda:

- 10:00-10:10: Introductions & scope (Grace)
- 10:10-10:30: SAML metadata ingest and test flow (Ben + Alex)
- 10:30-10:50: SCIM attribute mapping & group sync cadence (Ben)
- 10:50-11:05: Service-account provisioning, KMS rotation test plan (Neha)
- 11:05-11:15: IP allowlist change plan + rollback (Sally)
- 11:15-11:30: Q&A and action items

Pre-reads (please confirm before the call):
- medistruct_saml_scim_requirements.xlsx (filled copy)
- svcacct-mapping-v1.csv (Ben's mapping)

Action items before kickoff:
- Alex: share Okta metadata URL + KMS ARN (if you want rotation tests)
- Sally: confirm contact for emergency rollback during the window
- Grace: send calendar invite and attach the precheck runbook link

We'll capture minutes and assign owners in HubSpot after the call. Looking forward to it.

-Neha Kapoor
Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
